title.narrative: Establishing the basis for clean, healthy and resilient cities through an integrated and smart approach in Madagascar

description.narrative: Note: Disbursement data provided is cumulative and covers disbursement made by the project Agency.

The design of the child project has explicitly incorporated considerations of socio-economic benefits, clearly articulated within the project description. These benefits will be systematically monitored, evaluated, and reported during the Mid-Term Review (MTR) and Terminal Evaluation Report (TER). The project is strategically designed to deliver significant socio-economic benefits for the population of Toamasina, particularly targeting vulnerable and marginalized groups. Key socio-economic benefits include enhanced urban resilience, improved livelihoods, increased employment opportunities, and strengthened local governance capacity. Through targeted interventions, such as the establishment of smart infrastructure and the promotion of green economic activities, the project aims to substantially reduce vulnerabilities, especially among informal communities prone to climate risks. Economic opportunities generated through pilot investments in sustainable infrastructure, including waste-to-energy solutions, will specifically support job creation and economic inclusion for women and youth. Additionally, innovative financing mechanisms and capacity-building initiatives will directly benefit local enterprises, particularly micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs), facilitating their participation in new economic sectors such as recycling, renewable energy, and digital services. Enhanced digital governance platforms and participatory urban planning processes will amplify the socio-economic voice and decision-making capacities of previously marginalized groups, particularly women. By actively addressing digital divides, the project ensures broad-based inclusion and equitable access to project benefits, furthering social cohesion and community empowerment. Investments in essential urban services, such as improved waste management, sanitation, and public transport infrastructure, will notably elevate public health outcomes and quality of life for residents. Reduced pollution, strengthened environmental standards, and upgraded living conditions within informal settlements are anticipated to deliver tangible improvements in public health, community well-being, and overall urban sustainability. To ensure accountability and continuous improvement, socio-economic impacts will be rigorously tracked through clearly defined, sex-disaggregated, and context-sensitive indicators integrated into the project’s Monitoring and Evaluation framework. Reporting at key project milestones, including the MTR and TER, will comprehensively evaluate socio-economic outcomes, providing essential feedback for adaptive management and sustained benefit delivery throughout the project lifecycle.
Transformation of Toamasina into a model of clean, healthy, and resilient urban development, integrating smart technologies, sustainable infrastructure, and inclusive governance.
